prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To compute any classwide damages range you need: (1) Omega's actual share price immediately before and after each of the alleged corrective disclosures (July 27 and October 30-31, 2017), not just the percentage drops; (2) the number of Omega shares outstanding and the trading volume/number of shares purchased during the May 3-October 31, 2017 class period, to estimate the damaged share count; (3) an event-study or comparable methodology isolating the fraud-related portion of each price decline from general market or sector movement; and (4) ultimately a damages expert's per-share inflation estimate across the class period. None of these appear in the motion-to-dismiss opinion provided, which addresses only pleading sufficiency, not damages quantification.
prediction.likelyOutcome: At the Rule 12(b)(6)/PSLRA stage, expect a split ruling: the pure GAAP-misstatement theory and the undisclosed-loan omission theory (weak scienter, no identified corrective disclosure of the loan itself) are the most likely candidates for dismissal, while claims tied to the Q2/Q3 disclosures — where Omega's own admissions track closely with the 4% and 6.8% stock drops — have a better, though still contested, chance of surviving if plaintiffs can plead a specific misleading statement rather than just bad underlying business news. Section 20(a) liability will track whatever survives of the § 10(b) claim.

issues.label: §10(b)/Rule 10b-5 — Omission Theory (Undisclosed Working Capital Loan) and Materiality

outcome.description: After the district court dismissed the first amended complaint in 2019, the Second Circuit reversed in 2020 (968 F.3d 204), holding the non-disclosure of the working capital loan to the operator actionable and scienter adequately pleaded. On remand the court largely denied a renewed motion to dismiss (Sept. 28, 2021). The parties then settled; the court granted preliminary approval on December 27, 2022, and on April 25, 2023 entered an Order and Final Judgment approving a $30,750,000 cash settlement for the class of Omega securities purchasers (https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.484014/gov.uscourts.nysd.484014.167.0.pdf). Attorneys' fees were paid out of the settlement fund.
outcome.finalNote: Court-approved class settlement of $30.75 million (S.D.N.Y. Order and Final Judgment, ECF No. 167, April 25, 2023); fees came out of the fund; no appeal of the settlement.
